job.title: Registerd Nurse - Palliative Care
job.description:
This is a part-time position on a 0.6 FTE roster, and previous palliative care nursing experience is essential.

Join a growing team in a highly regarded hospice that supports the community and their whanau in a very sensitive time. With multiple programmes available, they are making a positive impact ono how this type of care is delivered to our loved ones.

What’s in it for you

  • Competitive salary
  • Part-time hours on a 0.6 FTE roster, with flexibility around how shifts are arranged
  • Professional development opportunities to build on your palliative care experience
  • A multidisciplinary team focused on providing thoughtful care to patients and whānau

About the role
You’ll care for people living with life-limiting illness, helping manage symptoms and providing comfort as their needs change. You’ll also support whānau through difficult conversations and help them understand what to expect as someone approaches the end of life.

You’ll assess patients, recognise changes in their condition and respond to symptoms such as pain, breathlessness and nausea. You’ll work with the wider team to adapt care plans around each patient’s goals and preferences, and provide clear documentation and handovers so care stays consistent across shifts.

What you’ll bring

  • You will be a New Zealand Registered Nurse and hold a current Annual Practising Certificate
  • Previous palliative care nursing experience in a hospice, hospital or community setting where caring for palliative patients was a regular part of your work
  • Confidence in symptom assessment and management, with sound judgement about when to escalate concerns
  • A calm, culturally responsive approach to working with patients and whānau
  • Availability to work a 0.6 FTE roster

Interested?
Apply with your CV, or call Robbie McKenzie at RWR Health on 09 520 7612 or 027 519 4993 for a confidential chat about the role and how the roster could work for you.

robbiem@rwrhealth.co.nz
www.rwrhealth.com

job.title: Nurse Practitioner
job.description:
About RWR Health & Nurse Practitioners
At RWR Health, we connect exceptional healthcare professionals with organisations that genuinely align with their career goals, values and lifestyle.

We take the time to understand what you're looking for and connect you with opportunities where you can develop professionally, feel supported and make a meaningful difference to the communities you serve.

We are currently looking to connect with a Nurse Practitioner to join a supportive and community-focused Primary Care team in South Auckland.

This is an opportunity to work within an established General Practice environment, providing high-quality, patient-centred care while working alongside an experienced multidisciplinary team.

The Opportunity
We are open to 3 or 5 days per week, providing flexibility to find a working pattern that suits your lifestyle and professional goals.

You'll work within a predominantly Māori and Pasifika community, providing accessible and culturally responsive Primary Care to patients and their whānau.

This could be an excellent opportunity for an NP who already has experience working within these communities, or someone with a genuine passion for developing their understanding and capability in Māori and Pasifika healthcare.

Why This Role Stands Out

  • Part time or full time options available
  • Work within a predominantly Māori & Pasifika community
  • Join a supportive and collaborative Primary Care environment
  • Deliver meaningful, patient-centred healthcare within your scope
  • Opportunity for continued professional development and career growth

Your Clinical Environment
You'll be part of a team that values collaboration, respect and quality patient care.

The practice has a strong focus on supporting the health and wellbeing of its local community, with culturally responsive care playing an important role in how services are delivered.

You'll have the opportunity to build strong relationships with patients and whānau while contributing to accessible and equitable healthcare.

About You
We're looking for a Nurse Practitioner who brings strong clinical skills, excellent communication and a genuine commitment to patient-centred care.

You will ideally have:

  • Current Nurse Practitioner registration with the Nursing Council of New Zealand
  • A current practising certificate
  • Experience within Primary Care
  • Excellent clinical assessment and decision-making skills
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills
  • A collaborative approach to multidisciplinary healthcare
  • A commitment to culturally responsive and equitable healthcare
  • An understanding of the health needs of Māori and Pasifika communities
  • A compassionate and patient-focused approach
  • Legal eligibility to work in New Zealand

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who is clinically capable, compassionate, community-minded and passionate about making a difference.

Your Development
You'll be joining an environment where professional development and continued learning are encouraged.

Whether you're an experienced Nurse Practitioner or looking to further establish yourself within Primary Care, this opportunity provides the support and clinical environment to continue developing your career.

Ready to Explore What's Next?
If you're a Nurse Practitioner looking for a supportive Primary Care environment, flexible working arrangements and the opportunity to make a genuine difference within a Māori and Pasifika community, I'd love to hear from you.

Not quite right for you?
Know someone who could be a great fit? We offer a $500 cash referral bonus for successful introductions.

job.title: General Practitioner
job.description:
About RWR Health & General Practice
At RWR Health, we connect exceptional healthcare professionals with organisations that genuinely align with their career goals, values and lifestyle.
We take the time to understand what you're looking for and connect you with opportunities where you can develop professionally, feel supported and make a meaningful difference to the communities you serve.

We are currently looking to connect with a GPEP3 Registrar or Fellowed General Practitioner interested in joining an established, community-focused Primary Care practice in South Auckland.

What makes this opportunity particularly interesting is the flexibility around how you shape your contribution. Whether your passion lies firmly in clinical practice and delivering excellent patient care, or you're looking to continue developing your leadership experience, there is room to explore both directions.

The Opportunity
You'll be joining an established General Practice serving a predominantly Māori and Pasifika community, working alongside an experienced team of GPs and a wider multidisciplinary healthcare team.

We recognise that not every GP wants the same thing from their career. Some are happiest focusing on their patients, developing strong clinical relationships and contributing through the quality of care they deliver. Others enjoy having a broader influence, supporting colleagues, sharing their experience and helping shape the future direction of a practice.

This opportunity can accommodate either approach.

Two Potential Pathways – One Great Opportunity
1. Clinical Focus | Make Your Impact Through Patient Care
If your preference is to focus on the clinical side of General Practice, you'll have the opportunity to:

  • Deliver high-quality, patient-centred care within an established Primary Care environment.
  • Build meaningful relationships with patients and whānau.
  • Work alongside experienced GPs and a supportive multidisciplinary team.
  • Contribute your clinical knowledge and experience to the wider practice.
  • Continue developing your own clinical interests and professional goals.

2. Clinical Leadership | Help Shape the Future of the Practice
If leadership is something you enjoy, or an area you'd like to continue developing, there is an opportunity to bring your experience and perspective to the wider practice.

You'll have the opportunity to work alongside an experienced team of GPs, helping articulate the practice's clinical direction and future development.

This is not necessarily about stepping into a traditional management position. Instead, you could become a trusted clinical advisor and source of support to the Practice Manager and wider health network.

Your contribution could include:

  • Providing clinical insight and guidance to support the Practice Manager.
  • Working alongside the GP team to identify opportunities for clinical improvement and development.
  • Helping shape the practice's future direction, standards and approach to patient care.
  • Supporting collaboration across the wider healthcare network.
  • Bringing your own leadership style, experience and clinical perspective to the team.

Importantly, the level of leadership involvement is something we would look to shape around your interests, experience and aspirations.

Your New Environment
The practice is part of a wider New Zealand healthcare organisation, providing access to a broader network of knowledge, experience and support.

However, what makes this structure appealing is that each clinic retains its own identity, personality and reputation. The direction of the practice is shaped by the people within it and the community it serves.

Rather than a centralised office dictating every change or setting a one-size-fits-all approach across the network, there is an emphasis on local ownership of the practice's identity, clinical approach and progression.

You'll be joining an organisation driven by patient outcomes and a genuine reflection of the communities its clinics serve.

Within this particular practice, you'll find an experienced GP team, a strong community focus and an opportunity to contribute to the continued development of an established service.

About You
We're interested in connecting with a GPEP3 Registrar or Fellowed General Practitioner who is passionate about delivering quality Primary Care and wants to be part of a supportive, collaborative team.

You'll ideally bring:

  • GPEP3 training or Fellowship with the RNZCGP.
  • Eligibility for registration and a current practising certificate in New Zealand.
  • A genuine passion for General Practice and patient-centred care.
  • Strong clinical assessment and decision-making skills.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building abilities.
  • A collaborative approach to working with colleagues and multidisciplinary teams.
  • An appreciation for culturally responsive healthcare and the needs of Māori and Pasifika communities.
  • An interest in contributing to the ongoing development of the practice, whether clinically or through leadership.
  • Also, for those looking for a blend of on-site and virtual settings to support your preferred way of working, all of this is possible within this organisation.

For those interested in the leadership pathway, previous experience supporting colleagues, contributing to clinical direction or working in a leadership capacity would be advantageous.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who wants to make a positive contribution and sees value in being part of a practice where their voice, experience and approach can genuinely make a difference.

Your Next Step
Whether you're a GPEP3 looking to establish yourself in an established Primary Care environment, a Fellow wanting to focus on clinical practice, or someone ready to explore a broader leadership contribution, this is an opportunity worth a conversation.

The direction isn't predetermined. We'd like to understand what you're looking for and explore how the role could align with your strengths, interests and longer-term career goals.

If this sounds like something you'd be interested in exploring, I'd love to hear from you.

Not quite right for you?

job.title: Youth Worker
job.description:
Bring your experience, build lasting relationships and become part of a community where your commitment matters.
Exclusive to RWR Health, we're partnering with Red Centre Support Services to recruit approximately 10 permanent Youth Workers for residential care services in Mount Isa, Queensland.
We're looking for people who will make the move, get involved in community life and provide consistent care. This is not a FIFO role or a fixed-term opportunity. We are looking for people who are committed to staying, building meaningful relationships and settling into both the work and the community.

The service and the young people
Red Centre provides 24/7 residential care for 26 children and young people aged 2–17 who have experienced complex trauma and require safety, stability and consistent adult support.

The service operates across nine residential houses, each accommodating up to four young people, depending on their individual circumstances and complexity of needs. Each house has a dedicated Team Leader, with most coming from teaching or youth work backgrounds.

The young people are predominantly from the Mount Isa community, and their whānau and families remain involved in their lives. Building and maintaining positive family relationships is a crucial part of the work. You'll need to understand the importance of family connection, work respectfully alongside whānau and recognise that supporting a young person also means recognising the wider relationships and community around them.

The young people have a range of complex backgrounds and support needs, which may include experiences of neglect, domestic and family violence, and sexual violence. Some also have additional learning and developmental needs, including ADHD, Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and developmental delays.
Challenging behaviours can be part of the day-to-day environment. You'll need to be confident, patient and emotionally resilient, with the ability to recognise triggers, respond appropriately to escalation and maintain a safe, consistent and supportive environment.

Much of the work happens through everyday life: preparing meals, supporting routines, attending appointments, encouraging positive activities and helping young people develop trust and confidence.

Culturally respectful care is central to the role. Many of the young people are Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, so you'll need to listen, learn and recognise the importance of identity, family, kinship, community and connection to Country.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Building trusting relationships and providing consistent, trauma-informed care.
  • Supporting daily routines, activities, appointments and individual care plans.
  • Helping children and young people develop practical skills, confidence and independence.
  • Building positive relationships with families and whānau and recognising their importance in each young person's life.
  • Recognising triggers and responding proactively to distress, complex needs and challenging behaviours.
  • Managing behavioural escalation while maintaining safety, appropriate boundaries and a calm approach.
  • Following individual safety plans, responding to incidents and maintaining accurate records.
  • Working alongside your Team Leader, colleagues and other services to support each young person's wellbeing.

What you'll bring
We're keen to hear from people with experience supporting young people in residential care, community services, mental health, alcohol and other drugs, youth justice or related settings.

Relevant qualifications may include Youth Work, Community Services, Mental Health, Alcohol and Other Drugs, Child, Youth and Family Intervention, Social Work, Counselling or Psychology. New Zealand qualifications will need to be assessed for recognition, and we'll help clarify whether your training meets the requirements.
You'll also need:

  • An understanding of trauma-informed care, child safety and professional boundaries.
  • Confidence supporting children and young people with complex trauma, developmental needs and challenging behaviours.
  • The emotional resilience and sound judgement to manage difficult situations, including behavioural escalation.
  • Strong relationship-building skills and an appreciation of the importance of family and whānau involvement.
  • Cultural awareness and a willingness to learn about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, culture and connection to Country.
  • A current, valid driver's licence.
  • Current First Aid and CPR certification, or willingness to obtain these before starting.
  • The ability to meet Queensland's Blue Card, screening and mandatory training requirements.
  • NZ Citizenship (or Australian work rights).

The service operates around the clock, so flexibility across days, evenings, overnight shifts, sleepovers, weekends and public holidays is essential.

Life in Mount Isa
Mount Isa is a remote, rural mining town in outback Queensland. While it has everything you need for day-to-day living, including supermarkets, shops, healthcare services, schools, sporting facilities, community groups, restaurants and local amenities, it's important to understand that this is a very different lifestyle from living in a major city.

The town has a strong mining and regional community feel, and getting involved in local sport, volunteering or community activities can be a great way to meet people and establish yourself.

The climate is another important consideration. Summers in Mount Isa are extremely hot, with temperatures regularly reaching very high levels. You'll need to be comfortable living and working in significant heat and prepared for the demands of an outback Queensland climate.

For those who enjoy the outdoors, there are opportunities for fishing, picnics at Lake Moondarra, local sporting activities and exploring the wider region.

This opportunity will suit someone who is genuinely open to a rural lifestyle, enjoys being part of a close-knit community and is prepared to make a longer-term commitment to both the role and the area.

Pay and support for your move

On offer is:

  • Flights to support your relocation
  • Three months' free accommodation
  • Access to a shared vehicle at the accommodation
  • Assistance finding a rental as you get established
  • Supported induction including cultural training and supervised buddy shifts
  • Opportunities to develop towards team leadership or management
  • Meaningful work supporting vulnerable young people
  • Permanent, full-time employment with fortnightly pay. This could range from $97,136 - $148,075 (base rate per annum) + 12% Super and will be confirmed based on the applicable award classification and pay point based on your qualifications and experience.
  • Shift penalties and allowances, including sleepovers are on top

job.title: Aged Care Registered Nurse
job.description:
Registered Nurse – Permanent Part-Time
Christchurch | $45–$47 per hour + shift allowances

Are you an experienced Registered Nurse with strong clinical skills and the confidence to lead a shift independently?
We are seeking a capable, proactive RN to join an independently operated retirement village and care facility in Christchurch, delivering high-quality, person-centred care to residents. This is an excellent opportunity for an RN who enjoys autonomy, takes pride in their clinical judgement and can confidently lead and support a team of care staff.

The Opportunity
The facility comprises 31 apartments offering a mix of care options, alongside a 25-bed hospital-level care facility. The wider village has a strong community feel, with a focus on providing compassionate care and maintaining residents' dignity, independence and wellbeing.

You will report directly to an experienced Clinical Manager with over 10 years of aged care experience, who has been with the facility since April. You'll also work alongside an experienced Unit Coordinator with over five years' experience across aged care and hospice.

The Clinical Manager works Monday to Friday until 5pm, while the Unit Coordinator works Tuesday to Saturday. There is always at least one RN on shift, and sometimes two. On Sundays, you will be the sole RN on duty, so confidence, sound clinical judgement and the ability to make independent decisions are essential.

You will be responsible for overseeing approximately 6–7 caregivers per shift, ensuring care is delivered safely, effectively and in line with residents' needs.
Roster and Remuneration This is a permanent, part-time position working three days per week on a rotating two-week roster.

Week 1

  • Sunday: 6:45am – 3:00pm
  • Monday: 2:45pm – 11:00pm
  • Tuesday: 2:45pm – 11:00pm
  • Total: 24 hours 45 minutes

Week 2

  • Sunday: 2:45pm – 11:00pm
  • Monday: 6:45am – 3:00pm
  • Tuesday: 6:45am – 3:00pm
  • Total: 24 hours 45 minutes

Each shift is 8 hours and 15 minutes, averaging 24 hours and 45 minutes per week across the two-week rotating roster.

Pay and benefits

  • $45–$47 per hour, depending on experience
  • Additional $6 per hour weekend allowance
  • Additional $3 per hour night shift allowance
  • Standard annual leave entitlement
  • Support from an experienced Clinical Manager and Unit Coordinator

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead shifts confidently, making independent clinical decisions and escalating concerns appropriately.
  • Oversee and support 6–7 caregivers per shift, delegating duties and prioritising workloads.
  • Assess residents' needs, develop and review individualised care plans, and monitor clinical outcomes.
  • Deliver nursing procedures safely and competently in accordance with best practice.
  • Maintain medication competency and ensure accurate clinical documentation.
  • Communicate effectively with residents, families, healthcare professionals and colleagues.
  • Maintain high standards of infection prevention and control, health and safety, and regulatory compliance.
  • Promote culturally safe, person-centred care and apply the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi in practice.

About You

We are looking for an experienced RN who brings a minimum of three years' experience working as a Registered Nurse in aged care and has the confidence to take ownership of a shift.

You will ideally have:

  • Current New Zealand Registered Nurse registration and a current practising certificate.
  • At least three years' aged care nursing experience.
  • Strong leadership skills and confidence supervising and directing care staff.
  • The ability to work autonomously, particularly when acting as the sole RN on Sundays.
  • Excellent clinical judgement, organisation and problem-solving skills.
  • A proactive, accountable approach and a commitment to high standards of care.
  • Strong communication skills and a compassionate, resident-focused attitude.
  • Experience with syringe drivers — ideal, but training can be provided.
  • Experience with VCare, 1Chart and InterRAI would be advantageous.

Why Apply?
You'll be joining a privately owned, independent retirement village and care facility that values quality, integrity, teamwork and genuine human connection.
You'll benefit from experienced clinical leadership and a supportive team, with the opportunity to use your clinical expertise, take ownership of your shifts and make a meaningful difference to residents' lives.

The organisation's values are Quality, Pride, Integrity, Teamwork and Laughter, underpinning its commitment to a positive, fulfilling experience of ageing.

Know someone suitable? We offer a $500 referral bonus for successful referrals.

job.title: Youth Worker - Relocate to Australia
job.description:
Youth Worker – Australia
Relocation Flights + three months’ free shared accommodation | Permanent, full-time | Mount Isa, Queensland

Make a difference and give yourself room to get ahead. You put your energy into helping others build a better future. Could it be time to make a move for your own?
If the cost of living is making it harder to get ahead, this could be an opportunity to reset. With flights and your first three months’ accommodation provided, you can take your youth work experience to Australia with support to get established.

Exclusive to RWR Health, we’re partnering with Red Centre Support Services to recruit full-time Youth Workers for residential care services in Mount Isa.

Meaningful work. A fresh start. You’ll support young people who need safety, stability and adults they can trust. Through everyday routines, shared activities and consistent encouragement, you’ll help them develop life skills, strengthen relationships and work towards their goals.
This is hands-on residential care. Some days will be challenging, and your ability to stay calm, maintain boundaries and respond thoughtfully will matter just as much as your enthusiasm.
Your work will include:

  • Building trusting relationships and providing consistent, trauma-informed support.
  • Supporting daily routines, activities and individual care plans.
  • Helping young people develop independence, confidence and community connections.
  • Responding to risks and incidents, with accurate case notes and reporting.
  • Working alongside colleagues and other services to support each young person’s wellbeing.

job.title: Service Delivery Manager
job.description:
$85,000-$110,000 per annum | Five weeks' annual leave
Napier office base | Leading community services across Hastings


About the organisation

Our client is an established community based disability support provider operating across the North Island. Their focus is simple but important - supporting disabled people to live the lives they choose, within their own communities.

Values led and people focused, they are passionate about delivering genuinely person centred services and building capable, well supported teams.

About the job

With the previous manager progressing into an internal quality role, an opportunity has opened to lead supported independent living services across Hastings.

Based in the Napier office (with some work from home flexibility), you will manage support workers who work alongside approximately 60-70 disabled people in their own homes and communities. Each person's goals, circumstances and support needs are different, making this a varied, hands-on operational leadership role.

Your time will be split between coordinating services and getting out into the community to coach staff, build relationships and engage with the people supported and their whānau. The administrative component includes the detail of rosters, referrals, documentation and planning. You will:

  • Coach and support a dispersed team, maintaining strong connections with staff who work independently
  • Coordinate rosters and respond to changing needs, matching people with support workers who suit their goals and preferences
  • Build relationships with community agencies, housing providers and other services to help people access the support they need
  • Work closely with needs assessment and referral teams, reviewing referrals and advocating for appropriate support hours
  • Oversee service quality, budgets, documentation and the safety of staff and people supported, including lone-worker risks
  • Strengthen referral relationships and support growth within the existing service

You will work closely with two other Hawke's Bay Service Delivery Managers, sharing ideas, connections and practical support. Occasional travel is required for induction and regional meetings.

About you

You understand community based services and know how to keep people connected, supported and accountable when they are working across different locations.

Your background could be in disability, mental health, social services, transitional support or disability employment services. You bring sound judgement, a practical approach and the confidence to work through changing priorities. You will have:

  • Experience leading teams, ideally with staff working independently in the community
  • Strong operational skills, including rostering, coordination and managing competing demands
  • The ability to coach staff, address performance concerns and build a positive team culture
  • Confidence building relationships across agencies and navigating community support
  • A commitment to disabled people's rights, choice and control, with culturally responsive practice
  • A relevant tertiary qualification or equivalent experience, including at least two years in health, disability or social services and at least one year managing a team
  • Confidence using digital systems, a full clean New Zealand driver's licence and willingness to travel occasionally

Existing Hawke's Bay networks would be valuable. If you are new to the region, your ability to build trusted community relationships will be equally important.

Benefits

  • $85,000 - $110,000 per annum, reflecting your experience.
  • Five weeks' annual leave.
  • Some flexibility to work from home.
  • Access to a shared pool car for work travel.
  • A structured induction, including time in Wellington with shared support teams.
  • Weekly coaching with your General Manager for the first three months, followed by ongoing regular support.
  • A close knit local management team and access to support from the previous manager.
  • An organisation that supports internal career progression.

If you enjoy bringing people, services and community connections together, apply now or contact Jeanette Rendle, Agency Director RWR Health Lower North Island ph 027 705 7079 for more information and / or a copy of the Job Description.

About the role

This 69-bed Hastings care home provides specialist dementia and psychogeriatric care across three secure wings. Its residents need more than well-managed services. They need a leader who understands complex care, champions dignity and helps staff respond with patience, confidence and compassion.

The vacancy follows a previous manager’s internal promotion to another facility in the region. You’ll have an experienced colleague nearby who knows the home and its community. Together, you’ll support a continuum of care for residents as their needs change.

Reporting to the Regional Manager and working closely with the Clinical Service Manager, you’ll oversee the home’s people, operations, quality and financial performance.

Growing occupancy is a key priority. You’ll build strong relationships with referral partners and help families feel informed and supported when considering specialist care for their loved one.

Your responsibilities will include:

job.title: Clinical Nurse Manager
job.description:
Bring your clinical expertise, your ideas and your ability to bring people together. This is an opportunity to make a lasting difference to residents and the team caring for them.



About the organisation

This independently owned, established aged care provider in Hastings delivers rest home and hospital-level care, with a strong commitment to residents’ dignity, independence and wellbeing.

Holistic care is central to its approach. Te Whare Tapa Whā guides practice, recognising the physical, emotional, spiritual and whānau connections that help people live well. The team takes pride in providing a culturally safe, inclusive environment where residents’ identities, beliefs and choices are respected.

There is a willingness to invest in care beyond the essentials. Preventative wellness clinics, specialist wound care, exercise programmes and an on-site wellness centre reflect a commitment to helping residents enjoy the best possible quality of life.

About the role

Reporting to the Facility Manager, you will lead clinical care across a 62-bed service, supporting a capable RN team and the wider care team to deliver safe, consistent, person and whānau-centred care.

Your leadership will set the tone. By listening, communicating clearly and recognising good work, you will build confidence, strengthen collaboration and create a shared sense of direction.

There is scope to shape the role and put your ideas into practice. Planned developments include additional beds and technology to support bedside documentation, creating opportunities to improve how care is delivered.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Coaching and developing the clinical team, building a culture of respect, learning and accountability.
  • Overseeing clinical assessments, care planning and care delivery for residents with varied and sometimes complex needs.
  • Leading quality improvement, clinical risk management and ongoing audit readiness.
  • Embedding culturally safe practice and protecting residents’ rights.
  • Working closely with residents, whānau, GPs and allied health professionals.
  • Leading change and strengthening systems, processes and follow-through.
  • This is a full-time position with a share of the on-call roster.


About you

You are an experienced clinical leader who combines sound judgement with warmth, approachability and clear expectations. You enjoy developing others, welcome ideas from your team and know how to turn improvement plans into everyday practice.

You will bring:

  • New Zealand Registered Nurse registration and a current Annual Practising Certificate.
  • Aged residential care experience and at least two years’ experience leading clinical teams.
  • Strong knowledge of quality, compliance and audit requirements, including Ngā Paerewa and the ARRC agreement.
  • interRAI competency and confidence using electronic clinical systems.
  • A commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi, culturally safe care and Te Whare Tapa Whā.
  • Experience leading change, with the organisation and initiative to see things through.
  • Above all, you will value the people around you - residents, whānau and colleagues - and understand the difference thoughtful leadership makes.



Benefits

  • $115,000 base salary.
  • KPI-based bonus, paid in quarterly instalments and linked to agreed measures
  • Support from an experienced Facility Manager, capable RNs with clinical portfolios and an experienced quality advisor.
  • Scope to influence clinical practice, introduce improvements and grow with the service.
  • On-site gym and wellness activities.
  • Staff meals and puppy daycare.

Ready to bring your leadership to a service where you can make a visible difference? Apply now, or contact Jeanette Rendle at RWR Health for a confidential conversation.

Join a collaborative rehabilitation team where your expertise helps people rebuild their lives after injury.

An exciting opportunity is available for a Registered Psychologist or Clinical Psychologist to join a well-established multidisciplinary rehabilitation provider in Timaru. Whether you're looking for full-time or part-time work (minimum 15 hours per week), you'll become part of a supportive team with an established caseload and strong clinical leadership.

job.title: Practice and Pastoral Lead
job.description:
Kaihautū Tū Manawa Ora | Practice and Pastoral Lead
Christchurch | Full-time, 40 hours per week | Four-year funded initiative

Lead with purpose. Support people. Create lasting change. Are you an experienced, people-focused leader passionate about strengthening practice, supporting workforce wellbeing and improving outcomes for tamariki, rangatahi and whānau?

This is an exciting opportunity to help shape a new initiative supporting children and families experiencing complex challenges across Waitaha Canterbury. This innovative, kaupapa Māori initiative brings together a multidisciplinary team to provide coordinated, culturally grounded and trauma-informed support to tamariki, rangatahi and whānau who need it most. They are looking for a relational and capable leader who can champion workforce wellbeing, develop practice capability and help establish a positive, reflective and supportive team culture from the ground up.

Ideally, you will bring a background in social work, counselling, teaching or a related profession, alongside experience in leadership, supervision or practice development. They are also open to candidates who bring exceptional kaupapa Māori knowledge, cultural capability and relevant leadership experience, even if they do not hold professional registration. Māori and Pasifika candidates are warmly encouraged to apply, with strong cultural knowledge, awareness and a genuine commitment to culturally grounded practice highly valued.

About the Role
As Kaihautū Tū Manawa Ora | Practice and Pastoral Lead, you will play a key role in developing the practice framework, supervision approach and workforce culture for a new initiative supporting tamariki and rangatahi aged 5–13 and their whānau.

The programme supports children and families experiencing complex challenges, including the impacts of parental imprisonment, school disengagement and intergenerational care experience. Support is delivered through a combination of hub-based and home-based services, with a focus on relationships, wellbeing and sustainable positive change.

Working collaboratively within the leadership team, you will help translate the programme's model of care into everyday practice, ensuring kaimahi feel supported, confident and equipped to deliver high-quality, whānau-centred services. This is an opportunity to help establish the foundations of a new service, influence team culture and ensure the people delivering frontline support have the guidance, resources and support they need to thrive.

The Team
You will be joining a developing multidisciplinary team with a shared commitment to improving outcomes for tamariki, rangatahi and whānau.
The leadership team will include a Quality Lead, with a teaching background, and a Kaupapa Lead, with a social work background. Together, they will help guide the programme's delivery, cultural integrity and practice standards. Alongside the leadership team, there will be eight kaimahi working directly with tamariki, rangatahi and whānau, including two Senior Practitioners who will bring additional experience and support to frontline service delivery.

As Practice and Pastoral Lead, you will play an important role in strengthening practice across the team, supporting kaimahi in their day-to-day work and fostering a culture of reflection, learning and wellbeing.

Key Responsibilities

  • Providing practice leadership, coaching and supervision to promote safe, reflective and trauma-informed practice.
  • Facilitating reflective practice sessions, team debriefs and collaborative learning.
  • Championing workforce wellbeing and fostering a psychologically safe, supportive team culture.
  • Supporting the development and implementation of practice frameworks and shared service delivery standards.
  • Strengthening multidisciplinary collaboration and coordinated support across hub and home environments.
  • Contributing to workforce coordination, rostering, onboarding and sustainable workload management.
  • Building positive relationships with whānau, community networks, education providers and partner organisations.
  • Supporting kaimahi to navigate complex situations and maintain strong, culturally responsive practice.
  • Contributing to shared leadership, continuous improvement and the successful establishment of the initiative.

Their Hours Reflect Their Kaupapa
They don't build their service around office hours; they build it around the lives of tamariki, rangatahi and whānau. This is a full-time position of 40 hours per week, with some flexibility required to support the needs of the service and its community. As part of the founding team, you will work collaboratively across a shared roster that includes daytime, evening and Saturday shifts. This helps ensure the service remains responsive, accessible and centred on whānau.

Hub operating hours:

  • Monday: 12.30pm – 6.00pm
  • Tuesday to Friday: 10.00am – 8.30pm (rostered shifts)
  • Saturday: 9.30am – 3.30pm (rostered shifts)

While the position is full-time, flexibility will be important to support occasional evening and weekend programme activities and the wider team's needs.

About You
You are an approachable, capable and culturally aware leader who understands the importance of strong relationships, reflective practice and supporting people working in emotionally demanding environments. You may come from a social work, counselling, teaching, clinical or related professional background, or have developed significant leadership and practice expertise through your experience working within kaupapa Māori, community or social services. They are looking for someone who can bring people together, build trust and help create an environment where kaimahi feel supported, valued and confident in their work.

You Will Ideally Bring

  • Relevant professional experience: A background in social work, counselling, teaching, clinical practice or a related discipline is preferred.
  • Leadership capability: Demonstrated experience within health, social services, education, community services or a similar environment.
  • Supervision and workforce support: Experience in coaching, pastoral leadership, practice development, staff supervision or workforce wellbeing.
  • Cultural knowledge and capability: A strong understanding of kaupapa Māori and culturally grounded approaches, with the ability to embed these into everyday practice.
  • Whānau-centred practice: A strong understanding of trauma-informed, relational and culturally responsive approaches to supporting tamariki, rangatahi and whānau.
  • Professional registration: Registration with a relevant professional body is welcomed but is not essential for the right candidate, particularly where they bring exceptional kaupapa Māori knowledge, cultural capability and relevant leadership experience.
  • Relationship-building: Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships across a diverse range of people and organisations.
  • Multidisciplinary collaboration: Experience working collaboratively across different professional disciplines or integrated service environments.
  • Adaptability and resilience: The ability to navigate complexity, balance competing priorities and adapt within a developing service.
  • Commitment to learning: A genuine willingness to reflect, grow and contribute to a positive team culture.
  • Practical requirements: A full New Zealand driver's licence and the ability to meet police vetting and relevant safety-checking requirements.

Māori and Pasifika candidates are warmly encouraged to apply. They value the cultural knowledge, perspectives and lived experience that can strengthen relationships with whānau and help ensure the service is grounded in the communities it supports.

Experience supporting vulnerable children, rangatahi and whānau is highly valued. Candidates with backgrounds in social work, counselling, teaching or related professions are encouraged to apply, particularly where they bring leadership, supervision or practice development experience.
Equally, they are interested in hearing from candidates who have developed exceptional kaupapa Māori expertise and strong leadership capability through their work in community, whānau or social services.

What's on Offer?

  • The opportunity to make a meaningful difference: Help establish an innovative initiative designed to improve outcomes for tamariki, rangatahi and whānau.
  • A role with purpose: Contribute to a service that places relationships, cultural grounding and whānau wellbeing at the heart of its work.
  • The opportunity to shape a new service: Help establish practice frameworks, develop team culture and influence how the programme operates from the ground up.
  • A collaborative leadership environment: Work alongside an experienced leadership team committed to kaupapa Māori and high-quality service delivery.
  • Full-time employment: A 40-hour working week, with flexibility to support programme requirements.
  • Four weeks of annual leave, plus eight additional mental health leave days annually after 12 months of service.
  • Professional registration support: Annual practising certificate renewal costs covered for relevant professional registrations.
  • Professional development: Support available after four weeks of employment.
  • Monthly individual supervision to support reflection, development and wellbeing.
  • Basic NIB health insurance.

Interested in Making a Difference? This is a unique opportunity to bring your leadership experience, cultural knowledge and passion for supporting people to a programme that places tamariki, rangatahi and whānau at its heart.
Whether you bring a professional background in social work, counselling, teaching or a related discipline, or have developed exceptional kaupapa Māori knowledge and leadership experience through your work in the community, they would love to hear from you.
If you are passionate about developing people, strengthening practice and creating a supportive environment where kaimahi and whānau can thrive, this could be the opportunity you've been looking for.


Know someone suitable? We offer a $500 referral bonus for successful referrals.
